chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Burayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
Regarding a mukatab for whom it was stipulated that if he became unable, he should be returned to slavery, he عليه السلام said: "The Muslims are bound by their conditions."

key_terms.شُرُوطِهِمْ: their stipulated conditions and contractual terms
key_terms.شُرِطَ: it was stipulated as a contractual condition
key_terms.عَجَزَ: he became unable to fulfill the obligation
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a contractual arrangement for emancipation
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْلِمُونَ: the Muslims, meaning the contracting parties within the Muslim community

ai.seo_question: Are Muslims legally bound by conditions stipulated in a mukataba contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mukatab, a slave under a contract of emancipation, where a condition was set that failure to fulfill the contract would result in return to slavery. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام states the general principle that Muslims are bound by their agreed conditions, affirming the legal force of such stipulations.
